name: The Azores: Sao Miguel, Pico and Faial

destination.name: The Azores: Sao Miguel, Pico and Faial
destination.pitch: Nine volcanic islands 1500 km out in the Atlantic where the walking, the water and the whales are the trip, and the cloud decides which of them you actually get.

because.nature: Crater lakes, lava coast and a 2351 m volcano, all within an hour of wherever you sleep.
because.exploration: Three islands in nine days, none of them more than 50 km end to end, and roads that reach almost everything.
because.food: Beef, limpets, fresh cheese and the best tuna in Portugal, cooked plainly; there are maybe six ambitious kitchens in the whole archipelago.
because.relaxation: Thermal pools at Furnas open until 23:00 and nothing at all to do after dinner anywhere else.
because.culture: Whaling that only stopped in 1984, a vineyard landscape of hand-built lava walls, and a town rebuilt after the 1980 earthquake.
because.adventure: Pico by the 47 poles, a lava tube in the dark, and boats that go looking for sperm whales.
because.city: Ponta Delgada holds about 45,000 people and you will have walked all of it before your second coffee.

destination.caveat: Cloud sits on the calderas and the summit of Pico for days at a time, so plan every big view twice, and each island hop costs you half a day between the drive, the check-in and the wait for a boat or plane that may not run. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Ponta Delgada
cities.base: The old town between Portas da Cidade and Campo de Sao Francisco, because it is the only place in the archipelago where you can eat well without driving, and the airport is seven minutes away for the

cities.name: Furnas
cities.base: Furnas village itself, within walking distance of the caldeiras and Poca da Dona Beija, so you can sit in the hot water at 21:00 instead of driving forty minutes back to Ponta Delgada in the dark.

cities.name: Madalena, Pico
cities.base: Madalena or Areia Larga just north of it, because the Faial ferry berth is in the middle of town and the mountain trailhead is forty minutes up the road; renting in the vineyards costs the same and pu

cities.name: Horta, Faial
cities.base: The strip between the marina and Porto Pim, so the bar, the museums, the beach and the ferry are all inside a ten minute walk and you only need the car for the Caldeira and Capelinhos.

cities.name: Angra do Heroismo, Terceira
cities.base: Inside the UNESCO grid between Praca Velha and the cathedral; this only fits in nine days if you give up a night on Pico or Faial, and it is a real trade rather than a bonus.

cities.name: Sete Cidades caldera
cities.base: No base. There are a handful of rooms in the village but nothing to do after dark and no petrol; sleep in Ponta Delgada and drive out at first light.

cities.name: Lagoa do Fogo
cities.base: No beds anywhere on the crater. It sits on the ridge halfway between Ponta Delgada and Furnas and you reach it from either in under forty minutes.

cities.name: Nordeste and the east coast
cities.base: A string of villages and clifftop viewpoints with almost no visitor beds; run it as a long loop out of Furnas, which is the closest bed by half an hour.

cities.name: Montanha do Pico
cities.base: Nothing to sleep in but the crater floor with a guide. Casa da Montanha at 1200 m is the trailhead and it is about forty minutes up from Madalena.

cities.name: Lajes do Pico
cities.base: A few rooms exist but the whole village eats and shuts early; the whale boats leave in the morning, so drive the forty five minutes from Madalena rather than moving your bags.

cities.name: Caldeira do Faial
cities.base: A crater and a car park at 1000 m, no beds and no shelter. Twenty five minutes up from Horta, and the road is often above the cloud base or inside it.

cities.name: Capelinhos
cities.base: An ash field where a village used to be, so there is nothing to sleep in; thirty five minutes from Horta by the south coast road.

cities.name: Algar do Carvao and the Terceira interior
cities.base: Moorland and lava caves in the middle of the island with no accommodation at all; twenty five minutes from Angra, and everything here opens only in the afternoon.

outings.name: the Sete Cidades rim walk
outings.why: Eleven and a half kilometres of caldera rim from Mata do Canario down to the village, with both lakes below you the whole way; it is linear, so you finish 30 km from your car and need a taxi, a second driver or the bus.
outings.season: All year, best May to September
outings.fallback: Drive to Lagoa do Canario and walk the twenty minutes to Boca do Inferno instead.

outings.name: Vista do Rei and the west coast loop
outings.why: Vista do Rei at opening, the village, then Mosteiros and the thermal sea inlet at Ponta da Ferraria timed to low tide; the whole thing hangs on the tide table and on the caldera being out of cloud.
outings.season: All year, Ferraria swimmable only near low tide
outings.fallback: Skip Ferraria and take the Mosteiros tidal pools and a long lunch.

outings.name: the Lagoa do Fogo descent
outings.why: Forty minutes down a steep clay path to the pale sand beach on the crater lake, an hour back up, then Caldeira Velha on the way out; no shade, no water and no phone signal on the descent.
outings.season: All year, path treacherous after heavy rain
outings.fallback: The two rim viewpoints from the car and a ninety minute slot at Caldeira Velha.

outings.name: the cozido lift at Lagoa das Furnas
outings.why: Watch the pots come out of the ground at the lakeshore late morning, then eat the thing in the village around midday; the meal is boiled meat and cabbage cooked by a volcano, so book it for the idea rather than the cooking.
outings.season: All year, lifted daily around the middle of the day
outings.fallback: Skip the lakeside crowd and just book the lunch.

outings.name: Salto do Prego from Faial da Terra
outings.why: A 4.5 km loop through laurel forest to a waterfall with a pool you can swim in, past the half-abandoned hamlet of Sanguinho; roots, mud and a steep first climb.
outings.season: All year, slow going November to March
outings.fallback: Drive to Ribeira dos Caldeiroes and walk the mill path for twenty minutes.

outings.name: the Nordeste viewpoint run
outings.why: Gorreana tea, Ribeira dos Caldeiroes, then the clifftop gardens at Ponta do Sossego and Ponta da Madrugada down the east coast; it is mostly driving and the road is slow, so it eats a full day.
outings.fallback: Gorreana and Ribeira dos Caldeiroes only, back in three hours.

outings.name: Pico summit
outings.why: 1150 metres of ascent from Casa da Montanha at 1200 m to Piquinho at 2351 m, marked by 47 poles, with scrambling on loose volcanic rock; roughly three and a half hours up and four down, registration and a GPS tracker are compulsory, and abo
outings.season: All year in theory, realistically May to October; closed on
outings.fallback: Walk up to pole 20 and back, or drive to Lagoa do Capitao and look at the mountain instead.

outings.name: the Criacao Velha vineyard walk
outings.why: Seven kilometres through the lava-walled currais that make up the UNESCO vineyard landscape, ending at the Moinho do Frade windmill; flat, entirely unshaded and blinding between 11:00 and 16:00.
outings.fallback: The Museu do Vinho and its dragon trees, forty minutes.

outings.name: the Lajes whale boat
outings.why: Three hours out of the old whaling port with clifftop spotters directing the boat; sperm whales are resident all year, the blue and fin whales pass in April and May, and it is cancelled outright when the sea gets up.
outings.season: April to October, best April and May for the big baleen whal
outings.fallback: The Museu dos Baleeiros in Lajes and the drive out to Ponta da Ilha.

outings.name: the Faial Caldeira rim
outings.why: Seven kilometres around the lip of a two kilometre crater, over Cabeco Gordo at 1043 m; exposed the whole way and the cloud comes in faster than you can walk out of it, so carry a GPS.
outings.season: All year, visibility best May to September
outings.fallback: The tunnel to the main viewpoint, twenty minutes, and hope for a gap in the cloud.

outings.name: Capelinhos and the Capelo coast
outings.why: The buried lighthouse, the underground museum about the 1957 eruption, and an hour walking on ash that still has almost nothing growing on it; the wind out here is constant and there is no shelter.
outings.season: All year, museum shut Mondays and Sundays November to March
outings.fallback: Museum only, then the Varadouro lava pools.

outings.name: the Ten Volcanoes trail
outings.why: Nineteen kilometres along the island spine from the Caldeira down over a chain of cinder cones to Capelinhos; linear, so you need a taxi at one end, and in fog you are navigating on a phone.
outings.fallback: The Caldeira rim loop, half the distance and the same view when it is clear.

outings.name: Angra and Monte Brasil on foot
outings.why: The UNESCO grid, the cathedral and the governors' palace, then the climb onto the volcanic headland that shelters the bay; parts of Monte Brasil are still army ground and gates shut without warning.
outings.fallback: The old town and the Duque da Terceira garden, two hours.

outings.name: Algar do Carvao and Furnas do Enxofre
outings.why: 338 steps down a volcanic chimney to a rain lake, then a boardwalk over sulphur vents on the moor above; everything here opens only in the afternoon and from October to March only four days a week.
outings.season: All year, afternoons only, Tuesday Wednesday Friday Saturday
outings.fallback: Serra do Cume and the Biscoitos lava pools instead.

places.name: Portas da Cidade
places.note: Three basalt arches that were the harbour gate until the seafront was filled in; you look for two minutes and then you are in the old town, which is the point.

places.name: Mercado da Graca
places.note: Pineapple, lupini beans, fresh cheese from Sao Jorge and a fish counter that tells you what the boats actually landed; Saturday is the real morning and the stalls thin out by 13:00.

places.name: Forte de Sao Bras and the Military Museum
places.note: A 16th century sea fort still owned by the army, with a dry collection of Azorean war history; go for the ramparts over the harbour rather than the cabinets.

places.name: Convento e Santuario da Esperanca
places.note: Home of the Senhor Santo Cristo image that the whole island processes behind in spring; the azulejo work in the lower choir is the reason to step in.

places.name: Museu Carlos Machado
places.note: Island natural history, sacred art and an old convent building; small, well lit, and the best forty minutes you can spend indoors when it rains.

places.name: Jardim Antonio Borges
places.note: A 19th century private garden gone slightly wild, with fig roots over a grotto tunnel; free, quiet, and five minutes uphill from the centre.

places.name: Gruta do Carvao
places.note: A lava tube under the edge of town, visited on fixed guided slots; book the same morning because groups are capped and the last slot fills first.

places.name: Tasquinha Vieira
places.note: Joel Vieira cooks island produce properly and the room holds maybe thirty people; they have gone back and forth on taking bookings, so turn up early rather than assume.

places.name: A Tasca
places.note: Petiscos, octopus, lapas and morcela in a loud tiled room; it is the default recommendation on the island, which means queues from 19:30 in summer.

places.name: Otaka
places.note: Nikkei cooking with Azorean fish, two seatings a night at roughly 18:30 and 21:00; confirm the times when you book because they shift with the season.

places.name: Louvre Michaelense
places.note: An old haberdashery turned cafe with the original fittings; good coffee, queijadas and no bookings, so go before 10:00 or after 15:00.

places.name: Portas do Mar
places.note: The cruise terminal strip of chain cafes and souvenir shops; when a ship is in it swamps the old town, and there is nothing here you cannot get better two streets inland.

places.name: Parque Terra Nostra
places.note: A 1780s botanical garden around an iron-orange thermal pool at about 38C; bring a dark swimsuit you do not love because the water stains, and go at opening to have the pool half empty.

places.name: Caldeiras das Furnas
places.note: Boiling mud pots and sulphur vents in the middle of the village, with taps of mineral water you can drink; ten minutes of looking, and the smell follows you back to the car.

places.name: Poca da Dona Beija
places.note: Five iron-rich pools around 39C, open to 23:00 and best after dark when the day trippers have gone; entry is capped at ninety minutes and costs more after 18:00.

places.name: The cozido holes at Lagoa das Furnas
places.note: Numbered pits in the lakeshore where restaurants bury their pots at dawn; the lifting happens late morning and is the free half of the meal, but the crowd around it is thick by 11:30.

places.name: Restaurante Tony's
places.note: The cozido everyone books, served from about 12:00; it is a plate of boiled meat and vegetables cooked in the ground, so order it once for what it is and not for refinement.

places.name: Mata-Jardim Jose do Canto
places.note: Camellias, redwoods and a neo-Gothic chapel on the lake shore; the quiet counterweight to the pot-lifting circus half a kilometre away.

places.name: Miradouro do Pico do Ferro
places.note: The whole Furnas bowl and its lake from above, ten minutes up a side road; cloud fills the valley most mornings before about 10:00, which is either the shot or the ruin of it.

places.name: Capela de Nossa Senhora das Vitorias
places.note: A neo-Gothic chapel built by Jose do Canto over his wife's tomb, with German stained glass; opening is tied to the garden ticket and it shuts in bad weather.

places.name: Miradouro do Salto do Cavalo
places.note: Furnas on one side, the north coast on the other, from a ridge that is in cloud more often than not; twelve minutes from the village and worth the gamble on a clear morning.

places.name: Furnas Boutique Hotel thermal spa
places.note: Indoor thermal circuit for the day the rain is horizontal; non-guests can book sessions but capacity is small, so call ahead rather than walking in.

places.name: A Terra
places.note: The one kitchen in Furnas doing island ingredients with some ambition; Furnas has perhaps four places serving dinner at all, so book the day you arrive.

places.name: Miradouro da Vista do Rei
places.note: The green lake and blue lake from the south rim, and the single most photographed spot in the Azores; it is in cloud roughly half of all mornings and the coach park fills from 10:00.

places.name: The Monte Palace hotel ruin
places.note: A concrete carcass of a 1989 hotel that closed after eighteen months; entering is trespassing, the floors are rotten, and from the road it is a stained slab in front of the view you came for.

places.name: Boca do Inferno
places.note: Twenty minutes of muddy forest track from the Lagoa do Canario car park to the rim notch that frames both lakes; better than Vista do Rei and you have to earn it slightly.

places.name: Lagoa do Canario
places.note: A small dark lake inside cryptomeria forest, and the parking for Boca do Inferno; the road in is narrow and rutted but any hire car manages it.

places.name: Lagoa de Santiago
places.note: A round crater lake below the rim road, two minutes from the car and usually ignored by everyone queuing at the next viewpoint.

places.name: Igreja de Sao Nicolau, Sete Cidades
places.note: The blue and white village church at the bottom of the caldera, where the rim walk ends; the village holds about eight hundred people and shuts early.

places.name: Cafe Lagoa Azul
places.note: Plain village cooking and cold beer at the end of the rim walk; it is a small kitchen with an unpredictable day off, so do not build the whole walk around eating here.

places.name: Piscinas naturais dos Mosteiros
places.note: Black rock tidal pools on the north west corner with four sea stacks offshore; swimmable only on a calm day and the Atlantic here does not stay calm for long.

places.name: Ponta da Ferraria
places.note: Thermal water bubbling into a sea inlet where you hold a rope against the swell; it only works around low tide, so check the tide table before you drive, and the free side gets crowded fast.

places.name: Miradouro do Pico da Barrosa
places.note: The high south viewpoint over Lagoa do Fogo; the crater makes its own weather and this is the first place to go white when a front comes in.

places.name: The Praia do Fogo descent
places.note: About forty minutes down a steep rutted path to the pale sand beach on the lake, and an hour back up; no shade, no water, and the top half is slick clay after rain.

places.name: Caldeira Velha
places.note: Warm iron pools and a waterfall inside tree fern forest, run on ninety minute timed slots with about a hundred places each; book two or three days ahead through the natural park site or you will not get in.

places.name: Miradouro da Lagoa do Fogo
places.note: Roadside pull-in on the Ribeira Grande side, lower than Pico da Barrosa and often clear when the top is not; parking is a narrow verge and it gets ugly at midday.

places.name: Cha Gorreana
places.note: Europe's oldest working tea plantation, family run since 1883, with free entry to the factory floor and a 3.3 km loop through the fields; the machines only run on weekday mornings.

places.name: Parque Natural da Ribeira dos Caldeiroes
places.note: Waterfalls, restored water mills and hydrangeas in a steep ravine beside the road; ten minutes of walking, and the lower falls are the one people photograph.

places.name: Miradouro da Ponta do Sossego
places.note: A terraced clifftop garden built by the local council in the 1980s, with cut lawns hanging over the sea; the best of a string of four viewpoints on this road.

places.name: Miradouro da Ponta da Madrugada
places.note: Faces due east, so it is the sunrise one if you are mad enough to drive ninety minutes in the dark from Ponta Delgada.

places.name: Salto do Prego
places.note: A 4.5 km loop from Faial da Terra through laurel forest to a waterfall you can swim under, passing the abandoned hamlet of Sanguinho; roots and mud most of the way and slow going after rain.

places.name: Farol do Arnel
places.note: A lighthouse at the bottom of a very steep concrete lane on the island's east tip; drive down only if your brakes and nerves are good, otherwise walk the twenty minutes.

places.name: Museu do Vinho do Pico
places.note: Wine making in the old Carmelite convent, with a grove of dragon trees over two hundred years old in the grounds; the dragon trees are the better half of the visit.

places.name: Cella Bar
places.note: A timber-clad building on the lava shore that won architecture prizes and now runs on wine, tapas and sunset; the terrace fills an hour before the sun goes and they do not take bookings for it.

places.name: O Ancoradouro
places.note: Fish soup and whatever the boats brought, at a table over the water looking at Faial; the single most reliable dinner on Pico and it books out a day or two ahead in summer.

places.name: The Criacao Velha vineyard walk
places.note: Seven kilometres through the UNESCO currais, the black lava walls built one stone at a time to shelter the vines, ending at the Moinho do Frade windmill; flat, exposed and blinding at midday.

places.name: Arcos do Cachorro
places.note: Sea arches and blowholes chewed out of the lava, with the old fishermen's cellars behind; slippery rock and no railings, so keep back from the edge when there is swell.

places.name: Lajido de Santa Luzia
places.note: The interpretation centre for the vineyard landscape, in a restored lajido settlement of black stone; small, clear, and it explains what you are looking at on the vineyard walk.

places.name: Gruta das Torres
places.note: The longest lava tube in Portugal, at roughly five kilometres, visited with a helmet and a lamp on a guided walk; tours are capped at fifteen or twenty people and the centre closes Sundays and Mondays in winter.

places.name: Furna de Frei Matias
places.note: A collapsed lava tube you can walk into with a torch, free and unstaffed; wet, uneven floor and no lighting at all, so it is a headtorch job or nothing.

places.name: Lagoa do Capitao
places.note: A shallow lake on the plateau with the mountain behind it when the mountain is out, which is maybe one morning in three; cows, bog and a dirt track in.

places.name: Museu da Industria Baleeira, Sao Roque
places.note: The old whale oil factory left standing with its boilers and presses in place; it processed sperm whales until 1981 and makes no attempt to make that comfortable.

places.name: Piscinas naturais da Madalena
places.note: Concrete steps and ladders into the lava pools on the edge of town, with Faial across the channel; no sand anywhere on Pico, so this is what swimming means here.

places.name: Casa da Montanha
places.note: Compulsory registration hut at the trailhead where you pay, sign in and are given a GPS tracker; numbers on the mountain are capped, so reserve a slot online before you fly.

places.name: The 47 poles
places.note: The route to the crater rim is marked by numbered poles from 1 to 47, hands needed on the rock in several places; about three and a half hours up and four down, and roughly a third of people turn back.

places.name: Piquinho
places.note: The last seventy metres is a separate scramble up the cone above the crater floor, with steam venting out of the rock at the top; in wind or cloud plenty of people stop at the rim and call that the summit.

places.name: The overnight on the crater floor
places.note: Guides run a sleep-on-the-mountain option so you are on Piquinho at sunrise; it is cold, hard ground and the cloud can still be sitting on you at 06:00.

places.name: The Lajes whale boat
places.note: Three hours out of the old whaling port, still directed from clifftop lookouts the way the hunt was; sperm whales are resident year round, the big baleen whales pass in April and May, and trips are cancelled outright on a rough sea.

places.name: Museu dos Baleeiros
places.note: Three boat sheds holding the open whaleboats that men rowed at sperm whales until 1984; the scrimshaw upstairs is better than the version sold to tourists in Horta.

places.name: Lajes waterfront and the Trindade church
places.note: The oldest settlement on Pico, a black stone seafront and a heavy baroque church; forty minutes covers it and there is nowhere to eat after about 21:00.

places.name: Ponta da Ilha
places.note: The far east end of Pico, a lighthouse on raw lava with vines growing out of it and Sao Jorge on the horizon; it is a fifty minute drive from Lajes and there is nothing in between.

places.name: The marina paintings
places.note: Every crew crossing the Atlantic paints its boat and date on the quay, and superstition says you get bad luck if you skip it; decades deep in places and free to walk end to end.

places.name: Peter Cafe Sport
places.note: The sailors' bar since 1918, which still holds mail for boats mid-crossing; the gin and tonic is the order, and between June and September it is full of people who arrived by plane.

places.name: Museu de Scrimshaw
places.note: One upstairs room of engraved sperm whale teeth and bone, most of it done by Azorean whalers; twenty minutes, closed Sundays, and it shuts at 16:00 on Saturdays.

places.name: Praia do Porto Pim
places.note: A sheltered sand bay inside an old crater, the only proper swimming beach in Horta and calm when the rest of the coast is not; walkable in ten minutes from the marina.

places.name: Fabrica da Baleia de Porto Pim
places.note: The whale oil factory that ran from 1942 to 1974, machinery intact, free to enter with a guided tour you must book ahead; winter hours are weekdays only.

places.name: Monte da Guia
places.note: A short climb onto the twin crater headland above Porto Pim, with the whole town, the channel and Pico laid out; a bit over an hour at a slow pace and exposed to the wind the whole way.

places.name: Museu da Horta
places.neighborhood: Largo Duque de Avila e Bolama
places.note: Regional history in an old Jesuit college, and a collection of miniatures carved from fig tree pith by Euclides Rosa that is genuinely unusual.

places.name: Canto da Doca
places.note: They bring raw fish, beef or squid and a slab of lava rock heated to searing, and you cook it yourself at the table; a gimmick that works, and booking is sensible from June onward.

places.name: Restaurante Genuino
places.note: Run by Genuino Madruga, who has sailed around the world twice alone; fish, limpets and a view west over the bay, and the kitchen keeps island hours so confirm the day.

places.name: Mercado Municipal da Horta
places.note: A small covered market with cheese, fish, fruit and two or three lunch counters inside; it is done by early afternoon and shut on Sundays.

places.name: Praia do Almoxarife
places.note: Black sand facing straight at Pico, eight minutes north of town; the water is colder and rougher than Porto Pim but this is where the view of the mountain is.

places.name: Miradouro de Nossa Senhora da Conceicao
places.note: A chapel on the hill behind town with the marina, Porto Pim and the channel below; ten minutes up on foot and the light is best in the hour before sunset.

places.name: The Caldeira viewpoint
places.note: A short tunnel from the car park opens onto a two kilometre wide crater four hundred metres deep, full of juniper and moss; on a bad day you see thirty metres of white and nothing else.

places.name: The Caldeira rim loop
places.note: Seven kilometres around the rim with about three hundred metres of up and down, over Cabeco Gordo at 1043 m; exposed, often muddy, and the fog arrives faster than you can walk out of it.

places.name: The guided descent into the Caldeira
places.note: Going down inside the crater is only legal with a certified guide and a natural park permit; a handful of operators run it and places are limited, so arrange it weeks ahead.

places.name: Centro de Interpretacao do Vulcao dos Capelinhos
places.note: Built underground so it does not spoil the ash field, covering the 1957 eruption that buried the coast and pushed a third of Faial's population to emigrate; closed Mondays and Sundays from November to March.

places.name: Farol dos Capelinhos
places.note: The lighthouse half buried in ash, left where the eruption stopped; you can climb the tower on the museum ticket and the wind at the top is serious.

places.name: The Capelinhos ash field walk
places.note: Grey and ochre cinder with almost nothing growing on it seventy years on; there is no shade, no shelter and the footing is loose, but it is the closest thing to walking on new ground in Europe.

places.name: The Ten Volcanoes trail
places.note: Roughly nineteen kilometres along the spine of the island from the Caldeira down to Capelinhos, over a line of cinder cones; it is linear, so you need a taxi or a second car at one end.

places.name: Piscinas do Varadouro
places.note: Sheltered lava pools on the south west coast, ten minutes from Capelinhos and the obvious place to wash the ash off; swimmable only when the swell is down.

places.name: Se de Angra do Heroismo
places.note: The cathedral of the Azores, rebuilt after a 1983 fire that gutted it; the town around it is UNESCO listed and was largely rebuilt after the same year's earthquake.

places.name: Palacio dos Capitaes Generais
places.note: The old governors' palace, where the Portuguese government sat in exile during the 1830s civil war; guided visits on a fixed timetable and closed Mondays.

places.name: Museu de Angra do Heroismo
places.note: A large regional museum in a convent, strong on the island's role as the Atlantic staging post for the Spanish and Portuguese fleets.

places.name: Monte Brasil
places.note: The volcanic headland that shelters the bay, with a road and trails up to the Pico das Cruzinhas cross; part of it is still an army base, so some gates are shut without notice.

places.name: Jardim Duque da Terceira
places.note: Terraced public garden on the slope above the old town, laid out in the 1880s; five minutes from everything and the best free shade in Angra.

places.name: Mercado Duque de Braganca
places.note: Terceira's covered market, busiest Friday and Saturday morning; cheese, alcatra beef and the sweet Dona Amelia cakes.

places.name: Quinta do Martelo
places.note: A reconstructed 19th century farm where they cook alcatra, the Terceira beef stew, in clay pots in a wood oven; it is a museum and a restaurant at once and needs booking.

places.name: Beira Mar
places.note: Straightforward grilled fish and limpets by the harbour; Angra keeps early hours and most kitchens stop serving around 22:00.

places.name: Prainha and the Angra bathing platforms
places.note: A small town beach and concrete sea platforms right under the old town; nothing special, but it is a ten minute walk from bed.

places.name: Miradouro da Serra do Cume
places.note: Looks down on the whole east of the island divided into a grid of green fields by black stone walls; twenty minutes from Angra and pure wind.

places.name: Piscinas naturais dos Biscoitos
places.note: Lava pools on the north coast with ladders and rails, the best sea bathing on Terceira; the north coast takes the swell, so a red flag day is common.

places.name: Museu do Vinho dos Biscoitos
places.note: The Brum family's verdelho cellar and small museum on the north coast, with a tasting at the end; short opening hours and shut at the start of the week.

places.name: Algar do Carvao
places.note: A volcanic chimney you walk down into, 338 steps to a rain lake at the bottom under silica stalactites; afternoons only, no reservations, and from October to March it opens Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Furnas do Enxofre
places.note: Sulphur fumaroles on open moorland with a boardwalk loop; free, five minutes from Algar do Carvao and usually windy enough that the smell does not linger.

places.name: Gruta do Natal
places.note: A 700 metre lava tube with a low, uneven floor, run by the same caving club as Algar do Carvao but ticketed separately; helmets provided and there is no combined ticket.
